question: Should OpenClaw permanently reserve the top-level `auth` CLI root even though plugins can currently advertise top-level command roots?
rationale: The shortcut's value is a product ergonomics choice, while accepting it changes a plugin-visible CLI namespace contract; removing the new root would also remove this PR's central feature.

options.title: Keep the plugin root available
options.body: Decline the shortcut and retain `openclaw models auth list` as the documented canonical command without changing plugin namespace behavior.

options.title: Reserve `auth` in core
options.body: Explicitly make `auth` a core-owned root, document the compatibility change, and require upgrade and installed-plugin collision proof before merge.

options.title: Design root composition first
options.body: Add a generic, maintainer-approved mechanism for core and plugin subcommands to coexist under one root before introducing the shortcut.

recommendation.title: Keep the plugin root available
recommendation.body: Decline the shortcut and retain `openclaw models auth list` as the documented canonical command without changing plugin namespace behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision directly affects the plugin CLI descriptor and overlap-guard contract introduced by their merged work.
